report:
PASS concerns the entire declared restricted scalar-Hopf A–G theorem, under the two exact task-granted BMP and gauge theorems. The unrestricted original P19 is not completed. I checked the current argument, the supplied reconstruction and their supporting proofs independently; previous verdicts, reading receipts and symbolic checks supply no premises.

A. The radial action is free and properly discontinuous. Polar coordinates give the compact connected smooth quotient S⁵×S¹. The charts z₀=eʷ establish the elliptic submersion and scalar E action. The complementary ranks of α and β prove h>0; differentiation gives dh=−ds∧α≠0. I inspected the indispensable [Xia–Zhang construction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.21053v1): heat estimates, completed-square estimate, transport and cutoff regimes, integrable negative deficit, and final smooth correction. These establish strict positivity while retaining divergent fiber energy on a fixed base ball. The quotient generators e and e⁻¹ define the same subgroup. Since D_source=2πD and ω=2πh, keep the potentials unchanged: h+Dφ=(ω+D_sourceφ)/(2π). The masses scale by (2π)⁻³. Each smooth potential is bounded individually, establishing v₊(h)=∞.

B. The smooth-background maximum argument is valid without closedness. For Fδ=δ log Σexp(wᵢ/δ) and pᵢ=exp(wᵢ/δ)/Σexp(wⱼ/δ), its exact Hessian identity is θ+DFδ=Σpᵢ(θ+Dwᵢ)+δ⁻¹Σpᵢd(wᵢ−Fδ)∧dᶜ(wᵢ−Fδ). The covariance term is positive. Convolution approximates the smooth background uniformly, and distributional passage retains the exact bound. Choquet selection and finite maxima containing a fixed integrable competitor therefore produce a genuine noncollapsed envelope.

On every local modification, the pulled sequence has a common quasi-psh bound, an integrable lower competitor and local L¹ convergence. Its canonical limit equals the pullback envelope off the exceptional locus, hence everywhere. Lelong semicontinuity preserves all divisorial lower constraints; domination of the fixed competitor supplies the reverse constraints. The ideal-order bounds and [Boucksom’s valuative criterion](https://sebastien.boucksom.perso.math.cnrs.fr/notes/L2.pdf) then retain every positive-real-weight ideal. The criterion requires one positive margin for all relevant divisors; separate strict inequalities are not substituted. Normalization, idempotence and nested-background composition follow from equality of competitor classes. Maximum with the admissible input also identifies the inclusion and equality envelope conventions used here.

The submersion assertion covers every holomorphic germ. Demailly’s tensor-product theorem applies on local product Stein disks with base weight tu/2 and fiber weight zero. Bounded smooth corrections preserve the ideals. Fubini on lifted germs reflects ideal equality downstairs. The reconstruction’s alternative Taylor–Parseval proof also checks: each coefficient belongs to the coherent base ideal, finite truncations belong to its extension, and Krull intersection in the finite module R/JR removes the remainder. Here R is the Noetherian convergent-germ ring and the proper ideal is generated by the fiber coordinates.

The full ambient competitor family is preserved by E. Its canonical envelope is therefore invariant and descends. In product coordinates, bh+DM=π*(bκ+Dw)+bβ. Smooth horizontal lifts annihilating β, tested against positive fiber densities, prove positivity of bκ+Dw distributionally. Local integrability and canonical uniqueness identify M=π*w including poles. Every base competitor lifts, proving both directions of the fiber-envelope identity over all ambient competitors.

G. Scalar invariance gives genuine normalized descents Γτ^(εh)=π*φτ^ε. The fiber identity makes them base ideal models. Scalar compatibility establishes equality of all positive-slice ideals at each fixed τ. For every positive smooth ξ, choose δκ≤ξ once for the whole interval and define Ψτ^ξ=P_(κ+ξ)[φτ^δ]_I. Feasibility gives nonemptiness; equality of scalar ideal classes gives independence of δ, scalar reproduction, normalization and compatibility, including for nonclosed ξ. Any compatible extension reproducing the scalar slices must equal these envelopes.

Maximum with the earlier input restores exactly the earlier divisorial data and proves decrease. For concavity, the intermediate input has orders no greater than the affine combination of endpoint orders. Maximum of the corresponding convex combination of competitors with that input restores every intermediate order. This proves whole-interval pointwise concavity, including exceptional divisors and canonical pole values; zero endpoint coefficients are omitted. Left constancy follows from the scalar inputs. The original genuine ambient limit descends to ψτ, and its model property gives the base model property. Bounds lκ≤k≤rκ imply φτ^(l/j)≤Ψτ^(k/j)≤φτ^(r/j), proving genuine decreasing limits independent of every auxiliary metric. Positive-slice ideals were not identified with limiting ideals in this construction.

C. Bounded κ-psh potentials have mass one, so the closed projective base has BMP. G establishes the full-system antecedent before the task-granted recovery theorem is applied. Positive initial lower ordinary-type volume therefore gives base recovery at every finite τ<c. The fiber identity gives scalar ambient recovery. For arbitrary η>0, choose εh≤η; original compatibility and nested-background composition yield Γτ^η=P_(h+η)[Γτ]_I. No finite upper-volume deficit on the Hopf manifold is used.

D. Uniform L¹ bounds for the normalized hyperplane logarithms make the negative series S genuine and noncollapsed. Both supplied proofs correctly normalize the total sum as ψ₀=S−sup S. The inputs satisfy κ+Duτ≥(1−λmax)κ and h+Dπ*uτ≥(1−λmax)h. All proposed families are consequently nonempty. Closure and the maximum arguments establish genuine models, normalization, compatibility, decrease, whole-interval concavity and left constancy.

Every local divisorial coefficient is λ(τ)Σqⱼord_F(Hⱼ), using the appropriate composite pullbacks upstairs. Canonical convergence of partial sums and countable additivity of positive current measures justify this formula on local modifications, including exceptional and accumulation-point divisors. The divisorial restriction formula excludes an additional accumulated divisor coefficient. Infinitely many positive distinct prime-divisor orders exclude both ordinary analytic singularity type and ideal-equivalent analytic data.

For each fixed input, decreasing perturbed envelopes dominate that input. Semicontinuity and domination retain exactly its orders, so their limits equal the unperturbed ideal envelopes. Scalar squeezing gives independence of every perturbing metric and canonical values at poles. Positive closed non-pluripolar multilinearity gives initial input mass at least (1−λ₀)². [Witt Nyström’s theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.01950v1) transfers this bound to the base model. Applying it in both ordinary-order directions gives the same mass for every ordinarily equivalent genuine competitor. Thus the initial lower ordinary-type volume is at least (1−λ₀)²>0. Together with A, this supplies the required nonanalytic recovery example with genuinely unbounded ambient upper mass.

E. At the exact pulled closed base background, every upstairs potential descends off the exceptional image. Locally bounded-above psh extension and canonical uniqueness establish descent everywhere, including exceptional poles. Surjectivity then reflects normalization and both ordinary-order inequalities, giving the complete competitor correspondence. Actual non-pluripolar measures agree on the isomorphism locus and charge neither exceptional analytic sets nor their images. Taking infima over all corresponding competitors preserves the transverse lower volume exactly. [Darvas–Xia Lemma 3.1](https://research.chalmers.se/publication/542539/file/542539_Fulltext.pdf) applies in its compact Kähler, closed big-background setting; the separately checked maximum argument identifies its inclusion envelope with the task’s equality envelope. The multiplier-ideal transformation retains the relative canonical/Jacobian correction. Arbitrary ambient modifications preserve the pulled local divisorial constraints; no nonclosed numerical-volume equality or recovery for new modified perturbation systems follows.

F. Gauge transport retains X, π, E, κ, α, β and the geometric metric h while replacing the background by h+Df. The strict potential −f verifies bigness. Transported normalized slices are the prescribed zero-obstacle ideal envelopes, rather than simple subtraction followed by an asserted model identity. The exact task-granted gauge theorem preserves the established recovery. Newly normalized gauged slices need not be basic. The classical positive-initial-ambient-lower-volume BMP branch remains distinct from the transverse branch. The valuative, envelope-concavity, modification, mass-monotonicity and Hopf-construction literature supplies substantial antecedents; no priority conclusion is asserted.

The four-line convention clarification is correct: ν_function(log|z|)=1, ν_function(log|f|²)=2ord(f), and the coefficient of [F] in Dφ is ν_function,F(φ)/2. With I(tu)=J(tu/2), the manuscript and reconstruction agree. The obsolete note’s instruction to scale Xia–Zhang’s potentials is wrong and explicitly superseded; the current argument requires no repair. Increasing envelopes converge through L¹ convergence and usc regularization, not necessarily through their raw pointwise supremum at every pole. No correction to total-sum normalization is needed.

Relevant primary statements and application contexts were freshly inspected. Where legacy PDF endpoints failed directly, their exact theorem pages were retrieved through indexed primary-source excerpts and checked against the supplied complete contexts; successful public mirrors were used for the published Darvas–Xia text and Demailly monograph. The last two passages record the exact task grants, which are excluded from the external-premise list.

Original unrestricted P19 remains unresolved: no general replacement invariant and uniform estimates beyond BMP, or specialization of a general new extension to the BMP theorem, have been established. Retaining the classical BMP branch separately does not discharge those obligations.

passages.statement: For a local psh φ, J(φ) defined using |f|²exp(−2φ), every prime divisor F over a smooth chart and every positive integer k satisfy ν_F(φ)−A(F)/k≤ord_F J(kφ)/k≤ν_F(φ), where ν(log|z|)=1 and A(F) is the finite log discrepancy.

For a psh φ near x on a smooth complex manifold and a nonzero holomorphic germ f, f∈J(φ)_x exactly when some ε>0 satisfies ord_F(f)≥(1+ε)ν_F(φ)−A(F) for every prime divisor F over a sufficiently small neighborhood whose center contains x; J uses exp(−2φ), ν(log|z|)=1, and one ε works for all such F.

For a psh φ near x on a smooth complex manifold and a nonzero holomorphic germ f, f∈J(φ)_x exactly when some ε>0 satisfies ord_F(f)≥(1+ε)ν_F(φ)−A(F) for every prime divisor F over a sufficiently small neighborhood whose center contains x; J uses exp(−2φ), ν(log|z|)=1, and one ε works for all such F.
For every local psh φ, the multiplier ideal I(φ) defined using |f|²exp(−φ) satisfies I(φ)=∪_{ε>0}I((1+ε)φ).
For local psh functions converging in L¹_loc, the limiting pointwise Lelong number is at least their limsup. Function Lelong numbers satisfy ν(max(u,v))=min(ν(u),ν(v)) and ν(u+v)=ν(u)+ν(v).

For a closed positive (1,1) current T, its generic Lelong number along a prime divisor F is the infimum of its pointwise numbers, and restriction of coefficient measures gives 1_F T=ν(T,F)[F], with ν([F],F)=1.
For a psh weight φ, J(φ), defined using exp(−2φ), is coherent; on a bounded Stein open set it is generated by any Hilbert basis of its weighted holomorphic L² space.
For complex manifolds X₁,X₂, psh weights φ₁,φ₂ and projections p_i, J(p₁*φ₁+p₂*φ₂)=p₁*J(φ₁)·p₂*J(φ₂) as ideal sheaves of all holomorphic germs, with J defined using exp(−2φ).
For a modification μ:Y→X of smooth complex manifolds and a psh φ on X, μ_*(O(K_Y/X)⊗J(φ∘μ))=J(φ), with J defined using exp(−2φ).

passages.statement: For a smooth modification μ:Y→X between compact Kähler manifolds, a smooth closed big background θ on X and u∈PSH(X,θ), Darvas–Xia Lemma 3.1 gives μ*P_θ[u]_I=P_(μ*θ)[μ*u]_I. Its source envelope uses v≤0 with I(tv)⊆I(tu) for every t>0, defines I(tu) using exp(−tu), and uses dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π).
The ring C{z₁,…,z_n} of convergent complex power-series germs is Noetherian.
For a Noetherian local ring R, a proper ideal I and a finite R-module M, ∩_{n≥0}I^nM=0.
A locally uniformly upper-bounded psh family has a countable subfamily with the same usc supremum; this supremum is psh and equals the raw supremum almost everywhere.

A distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable genuine psh representative. The psh cone is L¹_loc-closed and its L¹_loc-bounded families are relatively compact; a noncollapsed decreasing psh sequence has its genuine pointwise psh limit.
A psh function outside a closed pluripolar set extends uniquely across it if locally bounded above there.

For psh germs u,v at 0∈C^n, equality of their pointwise Lelong numbers at every point over 0 on every proper smooth modification is equivalent to J_+(tu)=J_+(tv) for every t>0, where J uses exp(−2φ) and J_+(φ) is the stationary value of J((1+ε)φ) as ε decreases to zero.

For a full compatible envelope system in a BMP background, positivity of the initial limiting lower ordinary-type volume implies recovery at every finite slice; the task grants this theorem for the full closed base system.
passages.quote: Under BMP, positivity of the initial limiting lower volume suffices: a finite upper-volume deficit gives stretches with uniformly controlled divisorial errors, and concavity propagates positivity to each finite slice.

passages.quote: Smooth gauge transport by theta prime=theta+dd^c f and Gamma prime=P_(theta prime)[Gamma-f]_I preserves recovery.
